clue.text: Jeopardise agreement with concessions

definitions.meaning: to put it at risk, as in compromising one's safety
a settlement in which each side gives ground

explanation.surface: A negotiator worries that giving ground might put the whole deal at risk.
explanation.definitionFit: The noun is a settlement where both parties yield something; the verb means to expose to danger or weaken.

clue.text: Conservative taunt or bluff

parts.note: to rag someone is to tease or taunt them

explanation.surface: A Tory politician's jibe might be a genuine insult or just a bluff.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bluff' looks like a verb about deceit, but here it is the noun for a steep cliff face.
explanation.definitionFit: A bluff is a steep headland or cliff, and a crag is a steep rugged rock face.

clue.text: Trade centres stocking some wild animals

indicators.note: markets stocking goods hold them inside, so one piece sits within the other

parts.note: marts are markets, places where trade is done

indicators.note: wild suggests the letters of 'some' run free into a new order

explanation.surface: Markets are found selling a few exotic creatures.
explanation.walkthrough: 'wild' scrambles the four letters to OMES; 'stocking' sets them inside the markets word. 'animals' is the plainest of definitions, hiding behind the zoo-trade surface.
explanation.definitionFit: Marmosets are small South American monkeys, so they are an example of animals.

clue.text: Get up about noon and wash

indicators.note: about means the first word goes round the other letter

parts.note: to rise is to get up out of bed

explanation.surface: A lazy morning: getting out of bed around midday and having a quick wash.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' puts N inside RISE.
explanation.definitionFit: To rinse is to clean something lightly with water, a kind of washing.

clue.text: Drove and tied up, keeping time

indicators.note: keeping means holding something inside, so one piece encloses the other

parts.note: a boat that is moored is tied up at its berth

explanation.surface: Someone drove to the harbour and secured their boat, all on schedule.
explanation.walkthrough: 'keeping' puts T inside MOORED.
explanation.definitionFit: To motor is to travel by car, so having motored is having driven somewhere.

clue.text: Put pressure on current boyfriend, perhaps

definitions.meaning: a 'main ...' or '...' is informal for one's current partner

explanation.surface: Someone is urged to lean on the man they're seeing at the moment.
explanation.definitionFit: Squeezing is pressing hard, literally or figuratively; as slang a squeeze is a romantic partner.

clue.text: Recognise as mostly crooked after reversal

indicators.note: after reversal tells us the shortened word is then read backwards
mostly means most but not all of the word, so its final letter is dropped

parts.note: something wonky is crooked or askew

explanation.surface: Someone recognises an object as largely bent once it has been turned round.
explanation.walkthrough: 'mostly' cuts WONKY to WONK; 'after reversal' turns that to the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: To know someone or something can mean to recognise or identify them.

clue.text: Demands nothing except energy, dedication and stamina at first

indicators.note: at first takes the opening letter of each of the listed words

explanation.surface: A job requires nothing but energy, dedication and stamina from the outset.
explanation.walkthrough: 'at first' takes the initials of nothing, except, energy, dedication and stamina; 'and' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Needs and demands are both requirements, here as plural nouns or third-person verbs.

clue.text: Aircraft research facility turn on bore

parts.note: to wind is to turn, as a key or handle
to tunnel is to bore through

explanation.surface: Instructions for switching on a drilling rig at an aviation lab.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down clue 'on' means the first piece sits on top of the second.
explanation.definitionFit: A wind tunnel blows air over model aircraft so engineers can study aerodynamics.

clue.text: Stole fruit, puzzled, with credit for time

indicators.note: credit for time means the credit letters stand in place of the time letter

parts.note: to be stumped is to be puzzled or baffled
CR is the accounting abbreviation for credit

explanation.surface: A thief, bewildered, bought something on account in place of serving a sentence.
explanation.walkthrough: 'for' swaps T out of STUMPED and puts CR in. Scrumping is a British word for stealing apples from orchards.
explanation.definitionFit: Scrumping is the British slang for pinching fruit, especially apples, from someone's orchard or tree.

clue.text: Garment from India prone to be revealing

indicators.note: to be revealing suggests the words disclose a word sitting within them

explanation.surface: An Indian piece of clothing that tends to show a little too much.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to be revealing' points to the letters spanning the end of India and the start of prone.
explanation.definitionFit: An apron is a protective piece of clothing tied over the front of other clothes.

clue.text: Staff turn once assembled outside hotel

indicators.note: outside means the rearranged letters wrap round the other letter
assembled means the letters are put together in a new arrangement

parts.note: H is Hotel in the NATO phonetic alphabet

explanation.surface: Hotel employees gather out front and rotate shifts.
explanation.walkthrough: 'assembled' rearranges TURN ONCE; 'outside' wraps that round H. 'Staff' looks like employees but is a stick.
explanation.definitionFit: A truncheon is a short club carried by police, a kind of stick or staff.

clue.text: Happen orbiter route occasionally goes off

parts.note: a comet is a body that orbits the sun

indicators.note: occasionally goes off means every other letter of the word departs, leaving the rest

explanation.surface: A satellite strays from its path every now and then.
explanation.walkthrough: 'occasionally goes off' drops alternate letters O and T from ROUTE, leaving RUE.
explanation.definitionFit: To come true is to be realised, as a wish or prediction that actually happens.

clue.text: Appearing in court, place will be distressed

parts.note: to be up before a court or magistrate is to appear there as a defendant
to set something is to place it

explanation.surface: Someone facing a judge will be anxious about where they stand.
explanation.definitionFit: Upset means troubled or emotionally disturbed, a synonym of distressed.

clue.text: Crosby, maybe having to repay son, flaps

parts.note: Bing Crosby was the American crooner; 'maybe' shows his first name is meant
money owing is still to be repaid
S is the genealogical abbreviation for son

explanation.surface: A famous crooner with a debt and a son flaps about it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'flaps' looks like a verb (panics) but is a noun. Bingo wings is British slang for loose flesh hanging from the upper arms.
explanation.definitionFit: Bingo wings are sagging folds of skin under the upper arm that wobble like flaps when waved.

clue.text: Independent church estate and country

parts.note: CE is the Church of England
an estate is landed property, i.e. land

explanation.surface: An independent church owns a rural estate and grounds.
explanation.definitionFit: Iceland is a Nordic island nation in the North Atlantic.

clue.text: Cut off a story with neat twists

parts.note: a story can be a fib or lie

indicators.note: twists suggests the letters are wrung into another order

explanation.surface: A tale with tidy plot turns is abruptly ended.
explanation.walkthrough: 'twists' rearranges NEAT to ATE.
explanation.definitionFit: To alienate someone is to isolate or estrange them, cutting them off from others.

clue.text: Account for one taken in by former scheme

parts.note: ex means former, as in ex-wife

indicators.note: taken in by means the single letter goes inside the following word

parts.note: a scheme is a plan
I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: Someone must justify being duped by an old plot.
explanation.walkthrough: 'taken in by' means the Roman one goes inside the scheme word, not inside the whole; 'one taken in' reads like a dupe on the surface.
explanation.definitionFit: To explain something is to give the reasons for it, accounting for it.

clue.text: Answer warnings and help, as previously mentioned

parts.note: 'Fore!' is the warning a golfer shouts, so fores are warnings
aid means help

explanation.surface: Respond to alerts and give assistance, as stated earlier.
explanation.walkthrough: A golfer shouts 'Fore!' to warn others of an incoming ball.
explanation.definitionFit: Aforesaid is a formal or legal adjective for something already stated or referred to earlier.

clue.text: Discussion group that's found in the kitchen?

parts.note: gas is informal for idle chat or talk
a ring is a group or circle of people

explanation.surface: A chatty circle of friends who always gather around the kitchen table.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark flags a definition by example: a cooking burner is one thing found in a kitchen.
explanation.definitionFit: A gas ring is a burner on a hob or cooker, a typical piece of kitchen equipment.

clue.text: Marvellous degree that's relative

parts.note: grand means splendid or marvellous
MA is a Master of Arts degree

explanation.surface: An impressive qualification that's all relative.
explanation.walkthrough: 'relative' looks like an adjective (comparative) but is the noun for a family member.
explanation.definitionFit: A grandmother is a family member, so a grandma is a relative.

clue.text: Hummer from California for robber?

definitions.note: the query marks an archaic or uncommon word for a thief

parts.note: LA is short for Los Angeles, the Californian city
a drone hums, as a bee or engine does

explanation.surface: A Hummer car from California used by a thief.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Hummer' looks like the brand of car but means anything that hums. A ladrone is an old word for a highwayman or thief.
explanation.definitionFit: Ladrone comes from the Spanish for thief and is an archaic word for a bandit or robber.

clue.text: Fails to cover scripture lessons for primates

indicators.note: to cover means the outer word goes over the other letters

parts.note: to lose is to fail, as in a contest
RI is religious instruction, school lessons in scripture

explanation.surface: A teacher neglects to cover the Bible class syllabus about apes.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to cover' means the failing word goes round the religious instruction letters; 'cover' reads on the surface as teaching a topic.
explanation.definitionFit: Lorises are slow-moving nocturnal primates of South and Southeast Asia.

clue.text: Sign on head of worried people such as these

definitions.note: plural people: the answer names a group, matching the plural 'these'

indicators.note: head of means the first letter of the word that follows

parts.note: an omen is a sign of things to come

explanation.surface: A notice above a worried face says something about these folk.
explanation.walkthrough: In an across clue 'on' places the sign after the initial W.
explanation.definitionFit: Women are people, and 'such as these' points to them as a kind of person.

clue.text: Send up notes on copyright

parts.note: mi is a note of the sol-fa scale, so two notes give MI MI
C is the copyright symbol

explanation.surface: A musician posts some sheet music with a copyright notice on it.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down clue 'on' puts the notes above the C.
explanation.definitionFit: To send someone up is to parody them, which is to mimic or imitate them mockingly.

clue.text: A day after game is cut short

indicators.note: after means the day letter follows the game

parts.note: bridge is a card game

explanation.surface: The day after a match, it is called off early.
explanation.definitionFit: Abridged means shortened or condensed, like an abridged edition of a book.

clue.text: Expensive to cross Belgium for hamper!

indicators.note: to cross means the outer word spans the letter, enclosing it

parts.note: dear means costly or expensive
B is the international vehicle registration for Belgium

explanation.surface: It's costly to take a picnic basket across Belgium.
explanation.walkthrough: 'hamper' looks like a picnic basket but is a verb meaning hinder.
explanation.definitionFit: To debar is to prevent or exclude, so it means to hinder or hamper.

clue.text: Bishop setting up organ bank for Scotland?

parts.note: B is the chess notation for bishop

indicators.note: in a down clue, setting up means the word is raised so it reads from the bottom upward

parts.note: the ear is an organ of hearing

explanation.surface: A clergyman establishes a body to set up a Scottish bank.
explanation.walkthrough: 'setting up' turns EAR upward in this down entry, giving RAE. 'bank' is a slope, not a lender.
explanation.definitionFit: Brae is the Scots word for a hillside or steep slope, which is a bank.

clue.text: Some, at end, must be fodder for worms

indicators.note: fodder suggests the words are material to be broken down and remade

explanation.surface: Some things, in the end, become food for worms.
explanation.walkthrough: 'must be fodder' rearranges SOME AT END. The surface plays on 'fodder for worms' meaning dead and buried.
explanation.definitionFit: Nematodes are roundworms, a large group of worms including many parasites.

clue.text: Bush's first retreat for Prime Minister

indicators.note: first takes the opening letter of the word before it

parts.note: a lair is a hideaway or retreat

explanation.surface: A president's first move is to pull back, for the sake of the UK leader.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface evokes George W. Bush and Tony Blair, allies over Iraq.
explanation.definitionFit: Tony Blair was UK Prime Minister from 1997 to 2007.

clue.text: Rifle fire

definitions.meaning: to ... a town is to plunder it, as rifle means to ransack
to ... an employee is to dismiss or fire them

explanation.definitionFit: Sack means both to plunder a place and to dismiss someone from employment.

clue.text: Loopy game may see card-castle collapsing!

indicators.note: a collapsing structure falls apart, so its letters are rebuilt in a new order

explanation.surface: A house of cards tumbling down might be a silly sort of game.
explanation.walkthrough: 'collapsing' rearranges CARD-CASTLE. 'Loopy' sounds like crazy but means made of loops.
explanation.definitionFit: Cat's cradle is a children's game of making figures from a loop of string on the fingers.
